newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ericsson, bonds drag Swedish shares to lower end.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson, bonds drag Swedish shares to lower end.

text.p: Swedish share prices closed lower on Monday, depressed by a fall in telecoms group Ericsson, higher long bond yields and a weaker U.S. bourse.
"Higher bond yields and worries about increased inflation depressed the bourse," a dealer said.
The Stockholm bourse's general index fell 0.56 percent to 3,140.76 in average turnover of 3.06 billion crowns.
Ericsson dropped 7.5 crowns to 354 after Finnish rival Nokia presented strong six-month figures and said its infrastructure order inflow clearly surpassed market growth.
"Worries about Nokia's success on (mobile) systems pulled Ericsson lower," a trader said, adding that this could mean that it Nokia has taken market share from Ericsson.
Truck maker Scania released a lower than expected six-month profit but rose 2.5 crowns to 227.5 as the company forecast an upturn on the sluggish European truck market.
Drugs major Astra rose 3.5 crowns to 145.5 ahead of releasing six-month figures on Friday, dealers said.
The forestry sector fell back 1.12 percent. Stora is due to release six-month earnings on Tuesday.
